title: Superflow vs Markup.io
kicker: · SUPERFLOW VS MARKUP.IO · THE AI QA REVIEWER FOR AGENCIES
headline: Markup.io is a feedback tool. Superflow is a feedback tool + a team.
secondary: The team is AI agents, built from your QA checklist. They check every site change and pin what they find. Your team decides. Your client approves from a link.
prevents: Stop finding every mistake by hand.
No more manual pass before launch.
qualifier: If your agency reviews client sites in Markup.io, this page is for you.
heroCaption: It's like Markup.io hired a QA team.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Markup.io was built before AI could check a site.
leftFacts: Agents run your checklist. Every change, desktop and mobile.
Findings land as pinned comments, rationale attached.
rightFacts: A person checks it. Nothing checks the site automatically.
No AI features found on markup.io, July 2026.
dimensions.verdict: A MarkUp is a record of what a person already caught. That's the part Superflow removes.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Feedback is easy to collect. A yes is harder.
leftFacts: Multi-step review flows: agents check, your team gates, then the client.
Your client opens a link and taps Approve. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.
rightFacts: Guests comment free from a link with no account.
Statuses plus a per-reviewer Sign off flow: Open for review, Editing content, On hold, Completed. Only Admins and owners set status.
dimensions.verdict: Markup.io's Sign off flow is real and per-reviewer, a genuine strength. Superflow's gate goes further: your team decides first, then the client approves, from their phone, no account.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: Comments on a copy are comments about the past.
leftFacts: Superflow lives on the site itself: passwords, Okta, SSO, no extension needed, guests included.
rightFacts: Renders the live URL through its own proxy, inside an iFrame.
Login-gated or iFrame-blocking sites can break, and may need the Chrome extension or a temporary auth change by your dev team.
dimensions.verdict: Markup.io reviews the live URL through a proxy render; Superflow reviews the site itself, behind logins and SSO, no extension.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal-only notes your team sees and the client never does.
The debate stays private; the client sees one settled answer.
rightFacts: Private MarkUps make a whole MarkUp private, a different concept.
Internal or private comments the client cannot see: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Renders as a difference only if the Markup.io side resolves to one.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both tools pin. The difference is what gets attached without asking.
leftFacts: Element and text pins, area comments.
A screenshot attaches to every comment automatically.
Recordings: screen, video, voice, from the toolbar.
rightFacts: Chrome extension auto-captures a screenshot on every comment or pin.
Auto screenshots without the extension: not yet verified.
Native video or screen recording: not yet verified. Loom integration attaches video.
dimensions.verdict: Pinning is even. Capture is the gap: Markup.io's auto-screenshot rides the Chrome extension. Superflow's attaches itself, no extension.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Boards hold tasks. They don't accumulate a client.
leftFacts: Brand rules and past decisions, learned once, fed to the agents next project.
rightFacts: No per-client memory or knowledge concept found: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: The tenth project should not start like the first.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The fix still has to ship.
leftFacts: Two-way Asana, Monday, ClickUp. Slack built in.
rightFacts: Workspaces, Folders, and Statuses on a dashboard. No kanban found.
Native Slack, Microsoft Teams, Loom, and Zapier, plus a public API with webhooks.
No native two-way sync: outbound only, via Zapier, the API, or webhooks.
dimensions.verdict: Markup.io has native Teams and Loom; Superflow doesn't today. If Teams or Loom is your spine, weigh that honestly. Markup.io's sync runs outbound only; Superflow's runs two-way.

pricingCompetitor: Verified July 2026: Pro is $79 per month, flat, unlimited users (admins, members, guests), 1 Workspace, unlimited MarkUps, 500GB storage, 100MB attachment cap. Enterprise custom, with SSO (SAML) and SOC II. Free tier after a 14-day trial, capped at 5 MarkUps and 10GB. Guests free.
switchingLines: One snippet on any site; one click on Webflow, WordPress, or GTM.
Paste the checklist you already have; agents assemble from it.
Open MarkUps finish in Markup.io. Nothing migrates on day one.
honestCloseStrengths: Markup.io earned its place. The price is flat: $79 a month, unlimited users, guests free. Guests join and comment from a link, no signup. Comment on 30 plus file types in one place: live websites, images, PDFs, videos. Statuses plus a per-reviewer Sign off flow track the work.
stayLine: If flat-price, link-based visual commenting on websites and files, with a simple statuses and sign-off flow, is all you need, Markup.io is a fine tool. Stay.

faq.question: Is Superflow just Markup.io with AI on top?
faq.answer: No. Markup.io files what a person found; Superflow's agents do the finding. A person makes every call.

faq.question: Do the agents replace my reviewers?
faq.answer: No. Agents run the first pass. Your team, then your client, signs off.

faq.question: What happens to our Markup.io projects?
faq.answer: Finish them in Markup.io. Start new work in Superflow. Nothing migrates on day one.

faq.question: Will our clients have to learn a new tool?
faq.answer: No. They get a link and an Approve button. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.

faq.question: Markup.io renders our client's site through a proxy. What if it blocks iFrames or sits behind a login?
faq.answer: Markup.io may need its Chrome extension or a temporary change to your login to work there. Superflow lives on the site itself, behind logins and SSO, no extension.
